payload.viable_set: The NO-REAL-ALTERNATIVES case, argued and recorded rather than manufactured. One candidate survives. The reason is that the architecture was ruled before this iteration opened - se-v2-design §4 specifies the two-parent filtered merge, the mandatory tag and the claim/event split - and this iteration's blessed rigor (se.decision-refine-mode) struck candidate generation for exactly that reason. Eleven implementation alternatives WERE enumerated and each was eliminated on a stated failure, not on taste: three breach the veto criterion or the invariant (merge-then-delete leaves the events in an intermediate commit, -s ours silently drops unlisted claims, tag-after-merge leaves an unnamed window), two are out of the binding scope, and the rest lose on ordinary-mechanics. Manufacturing a second survivor from that list would mean elaborating an option already known to fail a veto - the decision-theater hazard the design names. Recorded as degenerate, per the design's explicit allowance.
payload.complete_allocation: The single candidate allocates all thirteen functions with none orphaned: F1 -> the milestone lane on the bless path; F8 -> the pointer write, same path, separate concern; F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F9 -> the atomic close in shipMerge; F10 -> listing from the grant index; F11, F12 -> provisioning at open; F13 -> the standing constraint over the git invocation layer. INTERFACES: exactly one crosses clusters - the tag name - and it is deterministic (iter/<id>), so the bless path can write the pointer before the close path creates the tag, with no coordination. RATIONALE: the tear between the per-bless lane and the once-only atomic close is that they share no failure mode; a refused close must never be able to undo committed milestones.
payload.criteria_traced: Every criterion carries its requirement lineage: C1 nothing-lost from R6 and R11, weighted veto because the goal system ruled it outranks trunk-cleanliness; C2 trunk-clean from R5, the primary purpose; C3 permanent name from R3 and R4, high because C1 decays without it; C4 no-partial-state from Q1, R2 and R8, high because unattended operation makes a half-applied close the worst outcome; C5 ordinary-mechanics, medium, sourced from the git-maintainer role's tension - the repository must stay comprehensible without SE. The weights come from the requirement register and the four recorded stakeholder tensions, not from the candidate.
payload.front_recorded: A front of one, recorded as exactly that and not dressed as a comparison. Eleven eliminations, each with its reason: 1b more machinery for the same result; 1c invariant true only eventually; 1d silently drops unlisted claims; 2b cannot classify JSON evidence; 2c makes the invariant negotiable; 3b granularity below a milestone; 3c unrelated to any process boundary; 4b unnamed window; 4c requires moving a published tag; 5b reintroduces the clutter; 5c out of scope, it is i5e.
payload.feasibility_checked: Not rough - PROBED against real git before this gate (run-aa90b5a988e9), which is stronger than the state asks for. Confirmed: an empty branch is detectable; a branch can be tagged before its merge; a merge commit keeps two parents while its tree omits the event paths; the live claims merge correctly through the filter; withheld evidence is readable through the tag and absent from disk; and the pattern composes - a second close leaks nothing, the first iteration's evidence survives it, and a later merge does not resurrect the withheld paths. The only unexercised parts are UC-B (the milestone commit) and UC-D (provisioning), both build-time checks, and that gap is stated rather than hidden.
